notes: Recorded as "unknown" rather than true or false, deliberately. A VALUES-derived relation has no base-table attribution at all: PostgreSQL reports these columns with attrelid 0, so a catalog-driven analyser has nothing to look up and the question is out of scope for it -- which is precisely what FORMAT.md reserves "unknown" for, and it is scored like `true` so an engine that claims NOT NULL is still marked UNSOUND. Note the tension: for *this* particular VALUES list, both entries are non-null literals, so a sufficiently deep constant-folding analyser could legitimately prove NOT NULL, and `true` ("there exists a database state that makes it NULL") is strictly speaking not defensible either, since no database state is involved. "unknown" is the honest middle: undecidable-by-attribution, not provably nullable. Generalising is also unsafe -- a VALUES list with more than one row may contain NULL in any position. sqlx itself treats the columns of this query as nullable for the same attribution reason.
